summary: Vol. 11, No. 19, 12-page national edition of The Newark Herald (Newark, N.J.). Front page leads with the Gloucester County death sentences of Smiley Burrell and William Brown for the killing of William J. Horner, plus a Long Branch beach segregation ordinance fight and heavy Joe Louis-Max Schmeling fight buildup. Inside pages cover NJ church, club, NYA, NAACP and society news alongside national wire items on Marian Anderson, NAACP anti-lynching and anti-KKK campaigns, and entertainment/sports pages.

incidents.what: New Jersey appeals court denies final plea/rehearing for Smiley Burrell and William Brown, upholding death sentences for the hammer-slaying of William J. Horner in Gloucester County
Long Branch, N.J., adopts a beach ordinance restricting bathhouse access aimed at excluding Black residents from North Long Branch beaches; local committee and NAACP organize opposition
Joe Louis-Max Schmeling heavyweight title rematch scheduled at Yankee Stadium, New York, heavily previewed by Newark Herald
Arthur A. Schomburg, curator of the 135th Street library's Negro literature and history collection, dies in Brooklyn
Frank Burke, 12, of Trenton, N.J., nearly drowns and is saved from a canal
Home of Joel McClain in Dayton, Ohio, is bombed amid a housing/anti-discrimination demonstration dispute
Dillard University president Dr. William Stuart Nelson warns Lincoln (Mo.) University graduates against creeping dictatorship in a commencement address

connections: Newark Herald sports editor Lou Blackmon and managing editor Julius J. Adams cover both national Louis-Schmeling fight news and local NJ items, tying the paper into national Black press sports coverage
Coverage of the Long Branch, N.J., beach segregation ordinance explicitly ties local NJ civil-rights fight to NAACP involvement
Old Grads Return to Lincoln item connects Newark's Dr. H. H. Mitchell and Atlantic Highlands' Solomon P. Hood to Lincoln University alumni network, a recurring NJ Black press/education connection
